title: Don Wallace Steps Into the Spotlight: From New York Streets to Tubi's 'Stepfather'
htmlContent:
In the competitive landscape of Hollywood, few actors carry the kind of quiet confidence that comes from a lifetime spent grinding, learning, and showing up ready. Don Wallace is one of those actors. A native New Yorker with a magnetic screen presence, Wallace has steadily carved out a reputation as a go-to talent for law enforcement roles, gripping drama, and now, psychological thriller. With credits spanning NCIS: Los Angeles, The Family Business: New Orleans, All American, and The Rookie: Feds, Wallace is not just a familiar face—he is a proven commodity. And with his upcoming role in the Tubi original film Stepfather, he is poised to introduce himself to an entirely new audience in a major way.

A New Yorker's Journey to the Screen

Growing up in New York City has a way of shaping people in ways that money and privilege simply cannot replicate. The streets teach resilience, the culture breeds authenticity, and the chaos of city life demands that you stay sharp. For Don Wallace, those formative years in the Empire State became the bedrock of a performance style that feels lived-in and real. Audiences watching him on screen never have to wonder if he belongs—because he always does.

His work on NCIS: Los Angeles and The Rookie: Feds showcased a natural ease with authority figures and law enforcement characters, a niche Wallace has mastered and made entirely his own. That consistency of craft has not gone unnoticed in Hollywood's increasingly competitive television landscape.

Called Into Action by Director Chris Stokes

The road to Stepfather began with a collaboration that Wallace clearly holds in high regard. Director Chris Stokes, known for his ability to blend commercial entertainment with genuine emotional stakes, reached out to Wallace fresh off their work together on Hijack. The invitation to join the cast was not just a professional opportunity—it was a signal of trust and creative alignment. Speaking with LandonBuford.com, Wallace reflected on how the call came about:

Chris [Stokes] asked me to do this role right after we did Hijack, which was, you know, obviously for me I was very honored to like just be called out, hey, you know, kind of play this part, which is again law enforcement, which I'm familiar with."

That instinct—to return to what he knows, to lean into the authenticity of playing a law enforcement figure—is part of what makes Wallace's performances so effective. He does not merely perform authority; he inhabits it. And in the world of Stepfather, where danger lurks beneath the surface of what appears to be an ordinary domestic situation, that kind of grounded credibility is essential.

Chemistry With Taye Diggs on and off the Set

One of the most buzzworthy elements of Stepfather is its star-studded ensemble, led by the incomparable Taye Diggs in the role of Darnell/Leon/Kennedy—a desperate man whose obsessive search for the perfect family leads him down a dark and deadly path. For Wallace, getting to share scenes with Diggs was not just a professional milestone; it was a genuine personal highlight. Wallace opened up about the dynamic between the two actors:

"Working with Taye was just a dream, it was great. He's an amazing actor, very kind, and I'm basically interrogating him for certain misdeeds, if you will. I don't want to pull any spoilers there, but we had a really fun dynamic, and we actually got to hang out a few weeks after that at a friend's place. So, I mean, it was a fun time. It was easy, very easy set."

There is something deeply compelling about watching two skilled actors engage in an interrogation sequence, each one probing and defending, reading between the lines of what is said and what is left unsaid. The dynamic Wallace describes—an investigator closing in on a man whose secrets could shatter everything around him—promises to be one of the film's most riveting threads. And the fact that that on-set rapport extended naturally into a real-world friendship only speaks to the kind of atmosphere Stokes cultivates on his projects.

Inside the World of 'Stepfather'

Directed by Chris Stokes and written by Stokes alongside Marques Houston, Stepfather is a psychological horror thriller that taps into some of our most primal domestic fears. The film centers on a man who is consumed by the fantasy of building the perfect family—but when the women in his life begin to see through the carefully constructed facade, the stakes become life and death.

Produced by Footage Films Studios and edited by Harvey White, the film boasts a rich ensemble that includes Tamar Braxton as Asia, Kalani Jules, Jessica Jarrell as Melanie, Janeline Hayes as Detective Andrew, Dante Brown as John Simmons, Troy Brookins as Brett Dixon, TJ Shaw as Timothy, Koda Kalani Beschen as Brad Denton, and Elizabeth Dantus as Beverly.

The genre is a natural fit for the kind of layered, tension-filled storytelling that Stokes has long excelled at, and the casting of Diggs—an actor capable of projecting both irresistible charm and menacing instability—suggests a film willing to push its audience to the edge of their comfort zone. Wallace's role as an interrogating law enforcement officer places him squarely at the center of the moral reckoning the film promises to deliver.

What's Next for Don Wallace

With Stepfather set to land on Tubi and a portfolio of television credits that continues to grow, Don Wallace is at an inflection point in his career. The New Yorker who built his foundation on grit and authenticity now finds himself sharing the screen with some of entertainment's most recognizable names—and holding his own with ease. His comfort in front of the camera, his ability to find truth in a character even within the heightened reality of a thriller, and his obvious chemistry with collaborators all point to a performer whose best work may still be ahead of him.

For fans who have followed Wallace through his work on All American, NCIS: Los Angeles, and The Family Business: New Orleans, Stepfather offers a chance to see him operate in a different register—darker, more urgent, and more morally complex than anything he has tackled before. And for new viewers discovering him through Tubi's ever-expanding original content slate, consider this your introduction to one of Hollywood's most dependable and compelling character actors. Stepfather is coming. Don Wallace is ready.
excerpt: Actor Don Wallace, known for his work on NCIS: Los Angeles, All American, and The Rookie: Feds, opens up about his upcoming role in the Tubi original psychological thriller Stepfather, his collaboration with director Chris Stokes, and what it was like sharing scenes with Taye Diggs.
